$comment: Branding overlay rules for mold_v0 (mold_v0-024), read by .claude/scripts/branding.py. The codebase is never edited for an app: branding.py copies it to build/<app_id>/ and applies these rules to the copy, and every rule must match or the build is refused. NAME and WORDS go through the profile, never through source: the brand's fields are written into the copy's profile.json (the file scripts/gen-packs.mjs merges over the neutral default) and that generator is re-run, so src/profile.generated.ts and web/src/config/profile.generated.ts carry them (the MCP server name, the console's title and descriptions, the email sender's name). The tagline and description are written only when the brand has a tagline of its own; otherwise they are set to the shell's neutral words (`neutral`, gen-packs' DEFAULT_PROFILE), never left as the codebase's product's. `refuse`: characters the generator refuses in a name, so `set` and intake refuse them up front. The sender ADDRESS (email_from_address) is a mail-domain setting, not part of a brand: the overlay keeps it, and the app's profile settings (profile.app_settable, profile.email_defaults) write it. LOGO: the favicon set (lib/favicon.py) goes to the console's web/src/app (favicon.ico, icon.png, apple-icon.png, icon.svg for a vector mark only) and web/public (the manifest's 192, 512 and maskable PNGs), and manifest_icons points the web manifest at them. COLOUR: only the brand-carrying tokens (primary, its foreground, ring) of the console's one theme, light and dark; its neutrals stay the mold's. This overlay does not rewrite source code: since mold_v0-039 a product's landing page and pages are its host pack's, and the console's own text takes the profile's name.

neutral.console_description: Your workspace: connect an MCP client, run agents and read their results.
neutral.short_description: Connect an MCP client, run agents and read their results.

member_keys_off.$comment: mold_v0-116 (.claude/scripts/lib/app_profile.py): member_keys: false leaves signing in as the only way an AI client reaches /mcp, so it is refused at validation unless the codebase has one of these sign-ins for /mcp (the built-in OAuth server, or Clerk's). Whether the deployed app's sign-in actually works (Clerk's key on the API, Clerk letting clients register) is provision.py's check (mold.json mcp_sign_in).

email_defaults.$comment: mold_v0-101 (.claude/scripts/lib/app_profile.py email_defaults): what an app's build copy gets when the app's state sets neither email field and its host pack's profile does not either. from: the default sender's address, {notify_domain} being this machine's defaults.notify_domain (state/factory.local.json; none: no default, intake asks). notifications: the groups that are on (src/email.ts NOTIFICATION_GROUPS), plus due_dates when one of the app's packs declares a record area with due dates (pack.json record_areas[].due). The sender's name is the brand's.

app_limits_max.$comment: The highest value an app's own profile may give each limit named here (also inside a plan): a ceiling on what a brief or a state edit can raise. Raising one is a reviewed change to this file. The shell's defaults: runs.budget_usd_max 25, runs.kind_month_budget_usd 200, runs.concurrency_per_workspace 4, runs.live_per_workspace 20.

profile.$app_settable: The profile fields an app may set from its own state (application.json `profile`, mold_v0-090; .claude/scripts/lib/app_profile.py checks each and writes it into the build copy's profile.json over this mold's own). email and email_from_address since mold_v0-101 (the brief's ## Profile: email_from_address = <address>, email.notifications = <groups>). Never a brand word (the brand writes those), host_packs, source_offer.app, billing or entitlements. A dotted entry is one part of a field: source_offer.upstreams (mold_v0-099, the app's packs whose upstream is the licensor's own) while source_offer.app stays the factory's defaults.source_offer. member_keys (mold_v0-099): false turns per-member API keys off. legal (mold_v0-109): the company behind the app (company_name, contact_email, effective_date; optionally jurisdiction, terms_url, privacy_url), which turns on its /terms and /privacy pages and their links; intake asks a new app for it. mcp_instructions (mold_v0-119): what the MCP server tells AI clients about the app (plain text, up to 4000 characters), over its packs' pack.json mcp.instructions; the brief's ## MCP instructions section or a mcp_instructions line in ## Profile. landing (mold_v0-094): the app's landing page at /, over its pack's pack.json landing; the factory checks it as text (lib/app_profile.py landing_problems), the shell's build checks its sections (src/landing.ts); the brief's landing.<field> lines in ## Profile or a ## Landing JSON block. audit (mold_v0-197): the two audit trails, {"data": true|false, "platform": true|false, "retention_days": days}, each off unless true (the shell's src/audit-trail.ts; lib/app_profile.py audit_problems); with sign: true (mold_v0-195, src/ledger.ts) the hash-chained entries are signed in checkpoints every checkpoint_minutes (default 60) with APP_LEDGER_SIGNING_KEY from the app's environment. onprem_runners (mold_v0-205): true lets the app's workspaces install on-premises runners for the kinds that need their private network (the shell's src/onprem-runners.ts); absent or false (the default), no runner route, page, tab, MCP tool or enrolment exists and every run is hosted. features (mold_v0-219): one on/off flag per optional capability, {"<flag>": true|false}, the flags and their defaults in codebase/src/features.json (customer_key_vault, company_email, scheduled_alerts, record_clocks, audit.data, audit.platform, audit.sign, onprem_runners, developer_surface, declarative_checks, encrypted_fields, health_history, document_preview); a capability is on when something asks for it and its flag is not false; the legacy audit.* and onprem_runners keys still read and must agree (lib/features.py); the brief's features.<flag> = true|false lines in ## Profile.

share_image.$comment: mold_v0-093: the brand's own share image (what a shared link to the app shows), optional. Without one the console draws it from the profile's words, the landing page's headline, the mark and the brand colour (web/src/features/site/share-image.tsx). With one (branding.py <app_id> share-image <file>: the app's state records the file under brands/ and its sha256), `prepare` copies it to `file` in the build copy, byte for byte, and the generator (scripts/gen-packs.mjs) embeds it in web/src/config/share-image.generated.ts, which the console serves as it is at /opengraph-image and /twitter-image. A PNG of exactly width x height, at most max_bytes.

agent_icon.$comment: mold_v0-252: the workspace agent's own icon (the top bar's agent button and the agent pages' heading, while the profile turns agent_harness on), optional. Without one the console draws its default. With one (branding.py <app_id> set --agent-icon <file> | --agent-icon-name <name> [--agent-icon-dark <file>]; .claude/scripts/lib/agent_icon.py keeps it in the brand, a sanitised SVG or a PNG fitted inside 64 px, per theme), `prepare` writes light and dark files to `dir` and their addresses under `url` into the profile file's `profile_field` ({light, dark, mask}: mask when both are drawn in currentColor, painted in the text colour) before the mold's generator runs; scripts/gen-packs.mjs checks them and writes the field into the console's profile module only. A workspace owner may bring their own over it (Settings › Workspace agent, src/agent-icon.ts).

avatar_palette.$comment: mold_v0-275: the colours the console draws people's and organisations' avatars in when they have no uploaded picture (a soft gradient of two of them, chosen from the id, with white initials; web/src/components/identity-avatar.tsx). branding.py derives five from the brand colour at `set` (or the brand pins 3 to 8 of its own: set --avatar-colors), and `prepare` writes them as a list of #RRGGBB into the profile file's `profile_field` before the mold's generator runs; scripts/gen-packs.mjs checks them and writes them into the console's profile module only (`generated`). Without them (a brand with no colour, no brand) the console draws shades of its theme's primary colour (the theme's --avatar-1 to --avatar-5).
